title: Bali packing guide for men
description: What men should pack for Bali: temples, beach clubs and Ubud outfits, a packing list by trip length, and three budgets with real brands.
intro: Bali asks for two things: respect at the temple and ease at the beach. You will wear a sarong in one place and swim shorts in another, sometimes on the same day. Pack light, quick-dry layers, and one smart shirt. This guide covers temple dress, beach clubs, Ubud, a packing list by trip length, and three budget looks. It also covers the rain, because Bali has a wet season that surprises first-time visitors.

sections.heading: Temple dress, plainly
sections.body: Temples ask you to cover your knees and shoulders. Many give you a sarong and a sash at the gate, but carry your own. Wear a shirt with sleeves and trousers or a sarong. Remove your shoes if asked. Do not wear tank tops or short shorts. Stay out of the temple if you have an open cut. Be quiet and polite, and do not step over offerings on the ground. A light cotton shirt and a sarong cover everything.
tips: Cover knees and shoulders. Carry a sarong in your bag.
Wear a sleeved shirt and slip-on sandals.
Do not step on offerings or point your feet at shrines.

sections.heading: Climate note
sections.body: Bali is warm all year, around 27 to 32 degrees. The dry season runs from April to October. The wet season runs from November to March, with heavy afternoon rain and high humidity. Ubud and the highlands are cooler and wetter than the coast. Carry a light rain jacket year round. Choose quick-dry fabrics. Linen and thin cotton are ideal, and they pack light.

sections.heading: Packing list by trip length
sections.body: Laundry in Bali is cheap, so you do not need a lot. Plan to rewash every three days. Use packing cubes. Wear your heaviest items on the plane.
tips: 4 to 5 days: 4 tees, 2 shirts, 2 shorts, 1 trouser, 2 swim shorts, sarong, sandals, sneakers.
7 days: 5 tees, 3 shirts, 3 shorts, 1 trouser, 2 swim shorts, sarong, rain jacket, sandals, sneakers.
10 days: 6 tees, 4 shirts, 3 shorts, 2 trousers, 2 swim shorts, sarong, rain jacket, sandals, sneakers.
All trips: sunscreen, hat, plug adapter, a dry bag for the beach.

sections.heading: Three looks by budget
sections.body: Prices are approximate. Brands are on Myntra and Ajio. Choose breathable fabrics and muted colours.

pieces: H&M or Peter England light cotton shirt, about ₹1,000

looks.why: A sleeved cotton shirt with light trousers or a sarong covers temples and cafes.

looks.why: A linen shirt over swim shorts gets you into a beach club and a restaurant.

tips: Buy slip-on sandals. You remove them at every temple.
Choose a dry bag for the boat trip to Nusa Penida.

sections.heading: Wear on the plane
sections.body: Wear sneakers, light trousers, a cotton tee, and a light layer. Bali flights are long and the cabin is cold. Carry your sarong in your hand bag. Wear socks that you can remove. Pack your swim shorts in your carry-on, in case your bag is late. Keep your passport and the visa letter in a front pocket.

sections.heading: Ubud, beach clubs and rice terraces
sections.body: Ubud is cooler and greener, with cafes, yoga studios, and rice terraces. Wear a light cotton shirt, shorts or light trousers, and walking sandals. The Tegallalang walk has steps and mud, so choose shoes with grip. Beach clubs in Canggu and Uluwatu ask for a neat look: a linen shirt, swim shorts, and clean sandals pass everywhere. Sunset bars in Seminyak lean smarter, so bring one pair of chinos. Scooter rides need closed shoes and long pants, because road rash is the most common injury for visitors. Carry a light rain poncho, since the rain comes fast. Keep your phone in a waterproof pouch for the boat days.

sections.heading: What to stop buying
sections.body: Stop buying heavy trousers for Bali. Stop buying leather shoes. Stop buying a new swimsuit for each day. Stop buying souvenir tees at the airport. Buy a quality sarong in Ubud. It is cheaper and better.

faq.q: What should men wear to Bali temples?
faq.a: A shirt with sleeves, and trousers or a sarong covering the knees. Carry your own sarong.

faq.q: What should men pack for Bali?
faq.a: Quick-dry tees, linen shirts, shorts, swim shorts, a sarong, sandals, and a rain jacket.

faq.q: Can men wear shorts in Bali?
faq.a: Yes, on the beach and in towns. Not at temples, where you cover your knees.

faq.q: Is Bali hot in the wet season?
faq.a: It is warm and humid, with heavy rain in the afternoon. Pack quick-dry clothes and a rain jacket.
